hero.statement: I build software to understand how systems behave — then keep building until the thing in front of me does what it should. Mostly developer tools, desktop software and data work. Some of it is serious. Some of it started as a question.

home.workNote: Six projects, most from 2026. A browser built from scratch, tools for other developers, and a couple of experiments that got out of hand.
home.aboutBody: I'm a software engineering student who keeps building outside coursework — native desktop apps in Delphi, Python automation, web tooling, and lately AI woven into real workflows. I care most about the result being genuinely useful and understandable for the person on the other side.
home.contactBody: Recruiters, engineers, or anyone curious about one of these projects — the inbox is open.

about.title: About
about.lead: I'm a software engineer interested in building tools, systems and software that sit somewhere between engineering and experimentation.
body: It started as curiosity about software and turned into a habit of making things — turning an idea into something that runs, then improving the small details until it feels right. I've built automation tools, game logic, embedded experiments, and desktop and web applications, mostly in Delphi and Python.

What matters most to me is that the result is actually useful and clear for the person using it. My relationship with technology is about learning my way forward rather than consuming quickly — every project leaves me with something new, technically and otherwise.
